title: ROLE & CONTEXT
text:
ROLE & CONTEXT
Bạn là một chuyên gia lập trình web và phát triển tài liệu bằng Quarto. Mục tiêu dự án là xây dựng một website giáo dục chuyên nghiệp để lưu trữ và phân phối tài liệu học tập. Tính toàn vẹn của dữ liệu và không làm hỏng các trang đã hoàn thiện là ưu tiên TỐI THƯỢNG.


STRICT RULES FOR FILE MODIFICATION (QUY TẮC BẤT DI BẤT DỊCH)

TÔN TRỌNG TÍNH ĐỘC LẬP CỦA TỪNG TRANG (MODULARITY):


Khi được yêu cầu tạo hoặc chỉnh sửa một trang mới (ví dụ: tạo trang lý thuyết, bài tập), BẠN CHỈ ĐƯỢC PHÉP thao tác trên chính file .qmd của trang đó.
TUYỆT ĐỐI KHÔNG tự ý chỉnh sửa, định dạng lại, hoặc ghi đè lên các file .qmd của những trang khác đã hoàn thiện trước đó.


BẢO VỆ CÁC FILE CẤU HÌNH VÀ GLOBAL STYLES:


KHÔNG ĐƯỢC CHẠM VÀO file _quarto.yml trừ khi tôi có lệnh trực tiếp và rõ ràng: “Hãy cập nhật _quarto.yml”.
KHÔNG ĐƯỢC CHẠM VÀO các file CSS/SCSS dùng chung (ví dụ: styles.css, custom.scss). Nếu một trang mới cần định dạng đặc thù, hãy sử dụng thẻ <style> cục bộ ngay bên trong file .qmd đó, hoặc dùng các cấu trúc Div (:::) tiêu chuẩn của Quarto.


WORKFLOW XỬ LÝ YÊU CẦU:


Bước 1: Đọc kỹ yêu cầu và xác định chính xác những file nào MỚI CẦN tạo hoặc CẦN sửa.
Bước 2: Liệt kê ngắn gọn cho tôi biết bạn định chạm vào những file nào TRƯỚC KHI thực sự viết/sửa code.
Bước 3: Nếu yêu cầu của tôi buộc phải thay đổi một file dùng chung (như CSS tổng), bạn phải HỎI Ý KIẾN và CHỜ XÁC NHẬN từ tôi trước khi thực thi.


NHẬN DIỆN MÔI TRƯỜNG GIT:


Dự án này đang được quản lý bằng Git. Nếu bạn đề xuất các thay đổi lớn hoặc tái cấu trúc, hãy nhắc nhở tôi: “Hãy đảm bảo bạn đã git commit các trang cũ trước khi tôi thực hiện thao tác này.”

title: IB Chemistry Overview
text:
NoteIB Chemistry Syllabus Study Guidance



Welcome, students! This specialized IB Chemistry learning portal provides comprehensive resources aligned with the latest IBO curriculum, restructured around two core pillars: Structure (how matter is put together) and Reactivity (how matter behaves and reacts).

title: IB Chemistry Overview
text:
Choose Your Pathway
Select the appropriate program level below to access detailed study notes, syllabus-mapped practice questions, and key chemical formula guides:




IB Chemistry HL
Higher Level * Designed for students pursuing careers in Medicine, Pharmacy, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or Biology. * Covers all SL core topics plus Advanced Higher Level (AHL) modules in kinetics, equilibrium, thermodynamics, and complex organic chemistry. * Explore Resources →





IB Chemistry SL
Standard Level * Ideal for students seeking a fundamental natural science foundation or applying to business and social science programs. * Covers core concepts in atomic structure, chemical bonding, kinetics, and a basic introduction to organic chemistry. * Explore Resources →

title: IB Chemistry Overview
text:

This guide maps the specific 3rd-level learning objectives (Understandings, Applications, and Skills) of the 2025 IB Chemistry syllabus back to the legacy 2016 topics. This granular breakdown allows for exact file tagging (Notes, MCQs, Structured Questions) when migrating resource databases.
Note: Topics starting with 1x or 2x (e.g., 12, 13, 20) represent Higher Level (HL) material.

text:
NoteCourse Portal: AP Chemistry Prep



Chào mừng các em học sinh! Khu vực này chứa Sơ đồ kiến thức hóa học chuẩn đại học Mỹ, tóm tắt các phương trình điện hóa học, nhiệt hóa và cân bằng pH bằng LaTeX sắc nét cùng ngân hàng tài liệu luyện viết tự luận FRQ giúp đạt điểm tuyệt đối 5/5.

title: AP Chemistry Prep
text:
1. Course Overview & Assessment

Advanced Placement (AP) Chemistry là kỳ thi hóa học chuẩn hóa quốc tế cấp đại cương của College Board Mỹ. Kỳ thi đòi hỏi tư tư duy giải quyết vấn đề định lượng cực mạnh, phân tích sâu sắc bản chất cấu trúc vật chất, động học, năng lượng phản ứng, cân bằng dung dịch axit-bazơ phức tạp và kỹ năng thí nghiệm thực tiễn.


Cấu Trúc Đề Thi (Assessment Outline)

Đề thi AP Chemistry gồm hai phần thi MCQ (50%) và tự luận FRQ (50%) bắt buộc sử dụng máy tính khoa học:






Thành phần thi (Section)


Số lượng câu hỏi


Thời gian làm bài


Chính sách sử dụng máy tính


Trọng số điểm






Section I: Multiple Choice (MCQ)


60 câu trắc nghiệm khách quan


1 tiếng 30 phút


Cho phép dùng máy tính khoa học


50%




Section II: Free Response (FRQ)


7 câu hỏi tự luận lớn (gồm 3 câu lớn và 4 câu nhỏ)


1 tiếng 45 phút


Cho phép dùng máy tính khoa học


50%

title: AP Chemistry Prep
text:
2. Detailed Curriculum Framework (Core Units)
Chương trình học gồm 9 Units cốt lõi theo chuẩn sơ đồ của College Board:






ImportantCác chuyên đề cốt lõi của AP Chemistry:




Atomic Structure and Properties (Cấu tạo nguyên tử - 7-9%): Phổ quang điện tử (PES), cấu hình electron orbital, tuần hoàn các nguyên tố.
Molecular and Ionic Compound Structure (Liên kết - 7-9%): Công thức Lewis, thuyết lai hóa orbital, độ âm điện phân cực liên kết.
Intermolecular Forces and Properties (Lực liên phân tử & Khí lý tưởng - 18-22%): Lực IMF London/lưỡng cực/hydrogen, giản đồ pha hóa học, định luật khí lý tưởng \(PV=nRT\), quang phổ học Beer-Lambert.
Chemical Reactions (Phản ứng hóa học - 7-9%): Stoichiometry nồng độ dung dịch, phản ứng axit-bazơ trung hòa, oxi hóa khử redox.
Kinetics (Động hóa học - 7-9%): Phương trình tốc độ phản ứng tổng quát, cơ chế phản ứng từng bước, phương trình tích phân tốc độ.
Thermodynamics (Nhiệt hóa học - 7-9%): Biến thiên Enthalpy \(\Delta H\), nhiệt dung riêng calorimetry, năng lượng liên kết Hess.
Equilibrium (Cân bằng hóa học - 7-9%): Cân bằng động hằng số \(K_c\), hằng số áp suất khí \(K_p\), nguyên lý Le Chatelier hằng số tích số tan \(K_{sp}\).
Acids and Bases (Axit và Bazơ - 11-15%): pH axit-bazơ yếu \(K_a/K_b\), dung dịch đệm đệm (Buffers), phản ứng chuẩn độ axit-bazơ.
Applications of Thermodynamics (Nhiệt hóa nâng cao & Điện hóa - 7-9%): Entropy thay đổi, năng lượng tự do Gibbs \(\Delta G\), pin điện hóa galvanic thế chuẩn \(E^{\ominus}\) và điện phân.

title: AP Chemistry Prep
text:
3. Key Formulas & Worked Examples
Công thức hóa học hiển thị sắc nét bằng LaTeX:

Định luật quang phổ Beer-Lambert (Beer-Lambert Law)
Tính toán nồng độ chất tan dựa trên độ hấp thụ ánh sáng của dung dịch: \[A = \epsilon \cdot b \cdot c\] Trong đó \(A\) là độ hấp thụ (không đơn vị), \(\epsilon\) là hệ số hấp thụ mol, \(b\) là chiều dày cuvet truyền ánh sáng (cm), \(c\) là nồng độ dung dịch (M).


Phương trình tích phân tốc độ phản ứng bậc một (First-Order integrated rate law)
Mô tả sự suy giảm nồng độ chất phản ứng theo thời gian: \[\ln[A]_t - \ln[A]_0 = -kt\] \[\text{Chu kỳ bán rã (Half-life): } t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} \approx \frac{0.693}{k}\]

title: AP Chemistry Prep
text:
4. FRQ Strategies & Common Pitfalls






TipCác bí quyết giành điểm tuyệt đối FRQ AP Chem:




⚠️ Lý giải bằng lực liên phân tử (IMF) chứ không ghi tên liên kết: Khi được yêu cầu so sánh nhiệt độ sôi (boiling points) hay áp suất hơi (vapor pressure) của các phân tử hữu cơ, học sinh rất hay mắc lỗi ghi tên liên kết. Hãy luôn viết rõ ràng: “Phân tử \(C_2H_5OH\) có lực liên kết hydrogen liên phân tử mạnh mẽ hơn lực London phân tán liên phân tử của \(CH_3OCH_3\), dẫn đến đòi hỏi nhiều năng lượng hơn để bứt phá liên kết, nên nhiệt độ sôi cao hơn.”
⚠️ Phân biệt khái niệm thế khử và pin tự phát:

Sức điện động của pin tự phát \(E_{cell}^{\ominus} > 0\) thì năng lượng tự do Gibbs \(\Delta G^{\ominus} = -nFE_{cell}^{\ominus} < 0\).
Hãy luôn nhớ kiểm tra dấu âm/dương của hai đại lượng này để tránh mất điểm logic.

title: AP Chemistry Prep
text:
5. Topical Practice Questions (AP FRQ Bank)


Topic 1: Atomic Bonding & Beer’s Law

Đọc quang phổ PES, thuyết lai hóa orbital VSEPR và bài toán tính nồng độ quang phổ Beer-Lambert.
Tải đề luyện chuyên đề 1 →



Topic 2: Kinetics & Energy Rates

Luyện giải bài toán viết phương trình tốc độ phản ứng, tính toán chu kỳ bán rã và Hess’s Law.
Tải đề luyện chuyên đề 2 →



Topic 3: Buffers & titration curves

Tính toán pH dung dịch đệm, phân tích điểm tương đương đường cong chuẩn độ axit-bazơ.
Tải đề luyện chuyên đề 3 →



Topic 4: Electrochemistry & Gibbs

Tính toán thế chuẩn pin điện hóa, điện phân Faraday và mối liên hệ năng lượng Gibbs hằng số K.
Tải đề luyện chuyên đề 4 →

title: Edexcel IGCSE Science-Chemistry (4SD0)
text:
1. Course Introduction

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in Science (Double Award) (4SD0) is designed for students seeking a broad, dual-credit qualification in science. It encompasses core components of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics. The Chemistry component provides a thorough introduction to chemical structures, reactions, rates, energetics, and basic organic chemistry principles.


Assessment Outline (Chemistry Component)

The Chemistry component of the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in Science (Double Award) is assessed through a single externally examined paper. Calculators are permitted in the exam.






Assessment Paper


Target Curriculum


Format & Duration


Marks


Weighting (Chemistry)






Paper 1C (Chemistry Component)


Core Chemistry Syllabus Content


Written exam featuring multiple-choice, short-answer, calculations, and structured questions — 2 hours


110 marks


100% (33.3% of overall Science award)







Syllabus Structure

The Chemistry component is divided into 4 core areas:







NoteTopic 1: Principles of Chemistry





States of matter; elements, compounds, mixtures; atomic structure; the Periodic Table; calculations (stoichiometry); ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding.









NoteTopic 2: Inorganic Chemistry





Group 1 alkali metals; Group 7 halogens; gases in the atmosphere; reactivity series; extraction and uses of metals; acid-base reactions; chemical tests.









NoteTopic 3: Physical Chemistry





Energetics (enthalpy change); rates of reaction; reversible reactions and equilibria.









NoteTopic 4: Organic Chemistry





Terminology; crude oil (fractional distillation); alkanes, alkenes; synthetic addition polymers.

title: CIE IGCSE Science_Physics (0653 / 0654)
text:
1. Course Introduction

The Physics component of Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science (0653) and Co-ordinated Sciences (0654) covers fundamental principles of physics, mechanics, thermal physics, wave properties, electricity, electromagnetism, and space physics, preparing students to appreciate the physical world and technological applications.



Combined Science (0653): A single-award syllabus containing an equal mix of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics. It counts as a single IGCSE grade.


Co-ordinated Sciences (0654): A double-award syllabus featuring a more detailed, double-weighted coverage of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics. It counts as two IGCSE grades.



Assessment Outline (Physics Components)

Candidates who have studied the Core syllabus content are entered for Paper 1 (Multiple Choice), Paper 3 (Theory) and either Paper 5 (Practical) or Paper 6 (Alternative to Practical). Candidates who have studied the Extended syllabus content (Core + Supplement) are entered for Paper 2 (Multiple Choice), Paper 4 (Theory) and either Paper 5 or Paper 6.

Syllabus Structure

The Physics component comprises 6 major topic areas:







NoteTopic 1: Motion, Forces & Energy





Physical quantities and measurement techniques; motion; mass, weight and density; effects of forces; moments; energy, work and power; pressure.









NoteTopic 2: Thermal Physics





Kinetic particle model of matter; thermal properties and temperature; transfer of thermal energy (conduction, convection, radiation).









NoteTopic 3: Waves





General properties of waves; light (reflection, refraction, thin converging lenses); electromagnetic spectrum; sound.









NoteTopic 4: Electricity & Magnetism





Simple phenomena of magnetism; electrical quantities; electric circuits and electrical safety; electromagnetic effects.









NoteTopic 5: Nuclear Physics





The nuclear model of the atom; the nucleus; radioactivity (alpha, beta, gamma emissions, half-life, safety).









NoteTopic 6: Space Physics





The Solar System; stars and the Universe (Hubble constant, redshift, Big Bang theory).

title: Edexcel IGCSE Physics (4PH1)
text:
1. Course Introduction

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in Physics (Syllabus Code: 4PH1) is designed to provide students with a detailed understanding of the fundamental principles of physical science, motion, forces, electricity, waves, thermodynamics, magnetism, nuclear physics, and astrophysics. Through theoretical learning and practical investigations, candidates develop analytical problem-solving skills, preparing for further studies such as Edexcel International A-Level Physics or IB DP Physics.


Assessment Outline

The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE (9–1) in Physics (4PH1) is assessed through two externally examined papers. Both papers are taken at the end of the course. Scientific calculators are permitted in both examinations.

Syllabus Structure

The Edexcel IGCSE Physics syllabus is divided into 8 major topic areas, encompassing fundamental mechanics, energy, waves, electricity, atomic physics, and astrophysics:







NoteTopic 1: Forces and Motion





1a: Movement and position (speed, velocity, acceleration, distance-time and velocity-time graphs) 1b: Forces, movement, shape and momentum (Newton’s laws, stopping distances, terminal velocity) 1c: Momentum (conservation of momentum, impact forces, safety features) 1d: Moments (principle of moments, centre of gravity)









NoteTopic 2: Electricity





2a: Mains electricity (electrical safety, fuses, circuit breakers, earthing, power formulas) 2b: Current, potential difference and resistance in circuits (Ohm’s law, IV characteristics) 2c: Electrical components in series and parallel circuits (LDRs, thermistors, diodes) 2d: Static electricity (electric charge, electrostatic phenomena and applications)









NoteTopic 3: Waves





3a: Properties of waves (transverse and longitudinal waves, wave equation, Doppler effect) 3b: The electromagnetic spectrum (radio to gamma, uses and hazards) 3c: Light and sound (reflection, refraction, Snell’s law, total internal reflection, critical angle, sound waves and ultrasound)









NoteTopic 4: Energy Resources and Energy Transfers





4a: Energy stores and transfers (conservation of energy, Sankey diagrams, efficiency) 4b: Work, power and thermal energy transfers (conduction, convection, radiation) 4c: Energy resources (renewable and non-renewable energy generation)









NoteTopic 5: Solids, Liquids and Gases





5a: Density and pressure (calculating density, pressure in liquids and gases) 5b: Changes of state and specific heat capacity (heating curves, latent heat) 5c: Ideal gas molecules (absolute zero, Kelvin scale, Boyle’s law, pressure law)









NoteTopic 6: Magnetism and Electromagnetism





6a: Magnetism and magnetic fields (magnetic field lines, induced magnetism) 6b: Electromagnetism (magnetic effect of a current, motor effect, Fleming’s left-hand rule, electric motors) 6c: Electromagnetic induction (generators, transformers, transformer equations)









NoteTopic 7: Radioactivity and Particles





7a: Atomic structure and radiation (alpha, beta, gamma characteristics, decay equations) 7b: Radioactive decay, half-life, uses and dangers (contamination vs irradiation) 7c: Nuclear fission and nuclear fusion (nuclear reactors, chain reactions)









NoteTopic 8: Astrophysics





8a: Motion in the universe (gravitational field strength, orbital motion of planets, moons, comets) 8b: Stellar evolution (life cycle of solar mass stars and massive stars, Hertzsprung-Russell diagram) 8c: Cosmology (cosmic microwave background radiation, redshift, Doppler equation, Big Bang theory)

Welcome, students! This specialized section contains syllabus breakdowns, core study notes, targeted practice question banks, and actual exam past papers organized dynamically to optimize your learning and help you achieve a Grade 7.

title: IB Mathematics AI SL
text:
1. Course Introduction

Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (AI) Standard Level (SL) introduces students to the practical applications of mathematics in real-world contexts, modeling basic economic and physical systems, and foundational statistics and probability. It is designed for students interested in pursuing careers in Arts, Humanities, Social Sciences, Business, or Languages at the university level.


Assessment Outline

The IB Mathematics AI SL course is assessed through two final written examinations (80%) and an independent mathematical exploration task (20%). A graphic display calculator (GDC) is required for all written examinations:






Assessment Component


Duration


Calculator Policy


Marks

Independent research (12-20 pages)


No restrictions


20 marks


20%







Syllabus Structure

The syllabus is organized into five core topics at the standard level (Standard Level Core):







NoteTopic 1: Number and algebra





1.1: Operations in standard form 1.2: Arithmetic sequences and series 1.3: Geometric sequences and series 1.4: Financial applications 1.5: Laws of exponents with integer exponents 1.6: Approximation and significant figures 1.7: Amortization and annuities using technology 1.8: Systems of linear equations and polynomial solutions









NoteTopic 2: Functions





2.1: Straight lines: equations, gradient, intercepts 2.2: Concept of a function: domain, range, notation 2.3: Graphs of functions 2.4: Key features of graphs 2.5: Financial and modeling applications 2.6: Mathematical modeling process









NoteTopic 3: Geometry and trigonometry





3.1: Distance and midpoint in 3D space 3.2: Right-angled trigonometry 3.3: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle 3.4: Circle geometry: arc length and sector area 3.5: Equations of perpendicular bisectors 3.6: Voronoi diagrams









NoteTopic 4: Statistics and probability





4.1: Population, sampling, discrete and continuous data 4.2: Data presentation: frequency distributions 4.3: Measures of central tendency and dispersion 4.4: Bivariate data, correlation, and regression 4.5: Probability of events, Venn and tree diagrams 4.6: Independent and mutually exclusive events 4.7: Discrete random variables and expectation 4.8: Binomial distribution 4.9: Normal distribution 4.10: Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient 4.11: Chi-squared tests for independence and goodness of fit









NoteTopic 5: Calculus





5.1: Introduction to limits 5.2: Increasing and decreasing functions 5.3: Derivative of power functions and basic rules 5.4: Tangents and normals equations 5.5: Indefinite integration as anti-differentiation 5.6: Stationary points and local maximum/minimum 5.7: Optimization problems 5.8: Trapezoidal rule for approximating areas

NoteIB Mathematics Syllabus Guidance



Welcome to the IB Mathematics resource hub! The IB Diploma Programme Mathematics curriculum (first assessment 2021) is divided into two distinct pathways available at both Standard Level (SL) and Higher Level (HL): Analysis and Approaches (AA) and Applications and Interpretation (AI).

title: IB Mathematics Overview
text:
Choose Your IB Math Pathway
Select your course pathway below to access core syllabus revision notes, topical practice question banks, and formula booklet guides:




Math AA HL
Analysis & Approaches (HL) * Designed for students intending to pursue Mathematics, Engineering, Physics, or Computer Science at top universities. * Deep focus on algebraic rigor, calculus proofs, vectors, complex numbers, and advanced functions. * Explore Resources →





Math AA SL
Analysis & Approaches (SL) * Ideal for students pursuing Economics, Chemistry, Natural Sciences, or Pre-Med university courses. * Focuses on analytical methods, functions, trigonometry, differential & integral calculus, and statistics. * Explore Resources →





Math AI HL
Applications & Interpretation (HL) * Designed for students applying to Data Science, Business Analytics, Economics, or Social Sciences. * Emphasizes real-world mathematical modeling, technology integration, matrices, graph theory, and advanced statistics. * Explore Resources →





Math AI SL
Applications & Interpretation (SL) * Suitable for students seeking a broad practical foundation in mathematics or entering humanities and arts programs. * Covers statistical applications, financial mathematics, linear models, probability, and introductory calculus. * Explore Resources →

NoteCourse Portal: IB Mathematics AI HL (Applications & Interpretation)



Welcome, students! This specialized section contains syllabus breakdowns, core study notes, targeted practice question banks, and actual exam past papers organized dynamically to optimize your learning and help you achieve a Grade 7.

title: IB Mathematics AI HL
text:
1. Course Introduction

Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (AI) Higher Level (HL) focuses on the practical applications of mathematics in real-world contexts, modeling economic and physical systems, and advanced statistics and probability. It emphasizes the extensive use of technology and graphing software to solve complex, data-driven problems. It is highly recommended for students planning to pursue Economics, Finance, Data Science, Business, or Applied Sciences at top universities.


Assessment Outline

The IB Mathematics AI HL course is assessed through three final written examinations (80%) and an independent mathematical exploration task (20%). A graphic display calculator (GDC) is required for all written examinations:






Assessment Component


Duration


Calculator Policy


Marks


Weighting

55 marks


20%

Independent research (12-20 pages)


No restrictions


20 marks


20%







Syllabus Structure

The syllabus is organized into five core topics consisting of both standard core content and advanced high-level extension topics (SL Core & HL Extensions):







NoteTopic 1: Number and algebra





1.1: Operations in standard form 1.2: Arithmetic sequences and series 1.3: Geometric sequences and series 1.4: Financial applications 1.5: Laws of exponents with integer exponents 1.6: Approximation and significant figures 1.7: Amortization and annuities using technology 1.8: Systems of linear equations and polynomial solutions 1.9: Laws of logarithms [AHL] 1.10: Expressions with rational exponents [AHL] 1.11: Complex numbers in Cartesian form [AHL] 1.12: Polar and exponential forms of complex numbers [AHL] 1.13: Matrix operations and determinant [AHL] 1.14: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalization [AHL]









NoteTopic 2: Functions





2.1: Straight lines: equations, gradient, intercepts 2.2: Concept of a function: domain, range, notation 2.3: Graphs of functions 2.4: Key features of graphs 2.5: Financial and modeling applications 2.6: Mathematical modeling process 2.7: Composite and inverse functions [AHL] 2.8: Advanced graph transformations [AHL] 2.9: Modeling and fitting data [AHL]









NoteTopic 3: Geometry and trigonometry





3.1: Distance and midpoint in 3D space 3.2: Right-angled trigonometry 3.3: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle 3.4: Circle geometry: arc length and sector area 3.5: Equations of perpendicular bisectors 3.6: Voronoi diagrams 3.7: Logistic models [AHL] 3.8: Trigonometric definitions in unit circle [AHL] 3.9: Geometric transformations with matrices [AHL] 3.10: Concept of vectors [AHL] 3.11: Vector equations of lines [AHL] 3.12: Vector kinematics [AHL] 3.13: Scalar product and angle between vectors [AHL] 3.14: Graph theory: vertices, edges, degree [AHL] 3.15: Adjacency matrices and walks [AHL] 3.16: Algorithms for trees and cycles, MST, TSP [AHL]









NoteTopic 4: Statistics and probability





4.1: Population, sampling, discrete and continuous data 4.2: Data presentation: frequency distributions 4.3: Measures of central tendency and dispersion 4.4: Bivariate data, correlation, and regression 4.5: Probability of events, Venn and tree diagrams 4.6: Independent and mutually exclusive events 4.7: Discrete random variables and expectation 4.8: Binomial distribution 4.9: Normal distribution 4.10: Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient 4.11: Chi-squared tests for independence and goodness of fit 4.12: Data collection design and sampling [AHL] 4.13: Non-linear regression models [AHL] 4.14: Linear transformations of random variables [AHL] 4.15: Combinations of normal variables [AHL] 4.16: Confidence intervals [AHL] 4.17: Poisson distribution [AHL] 4.18: Hypothesis testing and critical regions [AHL]









NoteTopic 5: Calculus





5.1: Introduction to limits 5.2: Increasing and decreasing functions 5.3: Derivative of power functions and basic rules 5.4: Tangents and normals equations 5.5: Indefinite integration as anti-differentiation 5.6: Stationary points and local maximum/minimum 5.7: Optimization problems 5.8: Trapezoidal rule for approximating areas 5.9: Derivatives of standard functions [AHL] 5.10: Second derivative and concavity [AHL] 5.11: Indefinite and definite integration [AHL] 5.12: Volumes of revolution [AHL] 5.13: Differential equations and modeling [AHL] 5.14: Slope fields [AHL] 5.15: Euler’s method [AHL] 5.16: Coupled systems of differential equations [AHL]

1. Syllabus
The detailed syllabus structure for Edexcel Pure Mathematics 4 (P4) comprises the following topics:


1. Proof
1.1 Proof by contradiction.


2. Algebra and functions
2.1 Partial fractions.


3. Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
3.1 Parametric equations.


4. Binomial expansion
4.1 Binomial series for rational powers.


5. Differentiation
5.1 Implicit and parametric differentiation. 5.2 Simple differential equations.


6. Integration
6.1 Volume of revolution. 6.2 Integration by substitution and parts. 6.3 Integration using partial fractions. 6.4 Solving first order differential equations. 6.5 Area under parametric curves.


7. Vectors
7.1 2D and 3D vectors. 7.2 Magnitude of a vector. 7.3 Vector algebra. 7.4 Position vectors. 7.5 Distance between two points. 7.6 Vector equations of lines. 7.7 Scalar product and angles between lines.

title: Edexcel Pure Mathematics 1
text:
1. Syllabus
The detailed syllabus structure for Edexcel Pure Mathematics 1 (P1) comprises the following topics:


1. Algebra and functions
1.1 Laws of indices. 1.2 Surds. 1.3 Quadratic functions and graphs. 1.4 Discriminant. 1.5 Completing the square & solving quadratics. 1.6 Simultaneous equations. 1.7 Interpret inequalities graphically. 1.8 Represent inequalities graphically. 1.9 Solutions of inequalities. 1.10 Algebraic manipulation of polynomials. 1.11 Cubic and reciprocal functions. 1.12 Graph transformations.


2. Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
2.1 Equation of a straight line. 2.2 Parallel and perpendicular lines.


3. Trigonometry
3.1 Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area. 3.2 Radian measure. 3.3 Sine, cosine and tangent functions.


4. Differentiation
4.1 The derivative and rates of change. 4.2 Differentiation of polynomials. 4.3 Gradients, tangents and normals.


5. Integration
5.1 Indefinite integration. 5.2 Integration of polynomials.

title: Edexcel Mechanics 2
text:
1. Syllabus
The detailed syllabus structure for Edexcel Mechanics 2 (M2) comprises the following topics:


1. Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane
1.1 Motion under gravity. 1.2 Projectiles. 1.3 Variable acceleration.


2. Centres of mass
2.1 Centre of mass of discrete distributions. 2.2 Centre of mass of plane figures. 2.3 Equilibrium of a plane lamina.


3. Work and energy
3.1 Kinetic/potential energy, work, power and conservation.


4. Collisions
4.1 Impulse and conservation of momentum in vectors. 4.2 Direct impact and restitution.


5. Statics of rigid bodies
5.1 Moment of a force. 5.2 Equilibrium of rigid bodies.

title: Edexcel Probability & Statistics 1
text:
1. Syllabus
The detailed syllabus structure for Edexcel Statistics 1 (S1) comprises the following topics:


1. Mathematical models in probability and statistics
1.1 Basic ideas of mathematical modelling.


2. Representation and summary of data
2.1 Histograms, stem/leaf diagrams, box plots. 2.2 Measures of location. 2.3 Measures of dispersion. 2.4 Skewness and outliers.


3. Probability
3.1 Elementary and conditional probability. 3.2 Probability rules. 3.3 Independence. 3.4 Sum and product laws.


4. Correlation and regression
4.1 Scatter diagrams and linear regression. 4.2 Explanatory and response variables. 4.3 Product moment correlation coefficient.


5. Discrete random variables
5.1 Concept of a discrete random variable. 5.2 Probability and cumulative distribution functions. 5.3 Mean and variance. 5.4 Discrete uniform distribution.


6. The Normal distribution
6.1 The Normal distribution and cumulative tables.

Welcome, students! Advanced Level (A-Level) Mathematics is a highly respected qualification and a vital pathway for admission to prestigious global universities in STEM, Economics, and Finance.
NKK-Education Hub provides dedicated revision materials, topic-by-topic study notes, and fully interactive past exam paper banks for the three primary learning branches: CIE, Edexcel, and Other boards (such as AQA/OxfordAQA). Select your exam board below to get started.

title: A-Level Mathematics Overview
text:
Choose Your Exam Board
Select your specific exam board to access modular lesson sheets, step-by-step revision notes, and official exam archives with interactive search filters:




CIE Mathematics (9709)
Cambridge Assessment International Education

Academic curriculum divided into modular units.
Covers Pure Mathematics (P1, P2, P3), Mechanics (Paper 4), and Probability & Statistics (S1, S2).
Highly structured assessments emphasizing deep theoretical knowledge, mathematical proofs, and algebraic rigor.

Explore CIE Resources →





Edexcel Mathematics (IAL)
Pearson Edexcel International A-Level

Flexible modular assessment structure allowing students to sit exams in multiple series (January, June, October).
Covers Pure Mathematics (P1, P2, P3, P4), Mechanics (M1, M2), and Statistics (S1, S2).
Highly practical approach with exam questions focusing on real-world applications and calculator proficiency.

Explore Edexcel Resources →





Other Exam Boards (Others)
AQA, OxfordAQA, and General A-Level Curriculums

High-quality resources for students taking AQA, OxfordAQA, or equivalent general A-Level specifications.
Core math concepts aligned across all major international boards, focusing on Calculus, Algebra, and Data Interpretation.
Practice worksheets and generalized exam revision tools to reinforce exam readiness.

Welcome, students! This specialized academic portal provides in-depth resources for the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) curriculum. Here, you will find exhaustive syllabus checklists, revision notes, targeted practice question banks, and official exam information—all mathematically formatted to optimize your learning and help you achieve a Grade 9.

title: Edexcel IGCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
text:
1. Course Introduction

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A (4MA1) is a structured and comprehensive academic curriculum designed to develop mathematical skills, logical thinking, and problem-solving capabilities. The syllabus is divided into two tiers of entry: Foundation Tier (grades 5–1) and Higher Tier (grades 9–4, with grade 3 allowed), offering appropriate routes of assessment for students of different abilities.

Assessment Objectives (AOs) Weightings: * AO1 (Number and algebra): 57 - 63% * AO2 (Shape, space and measures): 22 - 28% * AO3 (Handling data): 12 - 18%


Syllabus Structure

The Edexcel IGCSE Mathematics A syllabus content is categorized into 6 major topics, covering core concepts for all students with extended high-level parts for the Higher Tier:







Note1. Numbers and the number system





1.1 Integers 1.2 Fractions 1.3 Decimals 1.4 Powers and roots 1.5 Set language and notation 1.6 Percentages 1.7 Ratio and proportion 1.8 Degree of accuracy 1.9 Standard form 1.10 Applying number 1.11 Electronic calculators









Note2. Equations, formulae and identities





2.1 Use of symbols 2.2 Algebraic manipulation 2.3 Expressions and formulae 2.4 Linear equations 2.5 Proportion (Higher Tier only) 2.6 Simultaneous linear equations 2.7 Quadratic equations 2.8 Inequalities









Note3. Sequences, functions and graphs





3.1 Sequences 3.2 Function notation (Higher Tier only) 3.3 Graphs 3.4 Calculus (Higher Tier only)









Note4. Geometry and trigonometry





4.1 Angles, lines and triangles 4.2 Polygons 4.3 Symmetry 4.4 Measures 4.5 Construction 4.6 Circle properties 4.7 Geometrical reasoning 4.8 Trigonometry and Pythagoras’ theorem 4.9 Mensuration / Mensuration of 2D shapes 4.10 3D shapes and volume 4.11 Similarity









Note5. Vectors and transformation geometry





5.1 Vectors (Higher Tier only) 5.2 Transformation geometry









Note6. Statistics and probability





6.1 Graphical representation of data 6.2 Statistical measures 6.3 Probability

text:
NoteSolid Foundation for Transition to IB / A-Level



Welcome, secondary students! The IGCSE Mathematics program plays an essential role in training logical mathematical thinking, mastering fundamental algebraic manipulations, and building academic English vocabulary. NKK-Education Hub provides detailed exam preparation resources and past papers for the most popular pathways: CIE 0580, CIE 0607 (International), and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1.

title: IGCSE Mathematics Overview
text:
Choose Your Exam Pathway
Select your specific exam curriculum below to go directly to its dedicated portal, featuring past papers, marking schemes, worked solutions, and key formula sheets:




CIE IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
Core Cambridge IGCSE Math Curriculum * Focus: Algebra, Geometry, Mensuration, Coordinate Geometry, Probability & Statistics. Categorized into Core (target grade C) and Extended (target grades A* to B). * Explore Resources (0580) →





CIE International Mathematics (0607)
Cambridge IGCSE International Math * Tailored for international schools incorporating Graphic Display Calculators (GDC) early. Focuses on technology-integrated problem solving and mathematical investigation. * Explore Resources (0607) →





Edexcel IGCSE Mathematics A (4MA1)
Pearson Edexcel IGCSE Math * Highly structured syllabus focusing on practical mathematical applications and strong pure algebra skills. Divided into Foundation and Higher tiers. * Explore Resources (4MA1) →

text:
📚 Curriculum Structure: CIE 9709 vs. Edexcel IAL

1. Cambridge Assessment International Education (CIE 9709)

Pure Mathematics 1 (P1): Quadratics, functions, coordinate geometry, circular measure, trigonometry, series, differentiation, and integration.
Pure Mathematics 3 (P3): Algebra, logarithmic/exponential functions, trigonometry, numerical solutions, vectors, differential equations, and complex numbers.
Mechanics (Paper 4 / M1): Forces and equilibrium, kinematics of motion, Newton’s laws of motion, work, energy, and power.
Probability & Statistics 1 (Paper 5 / S1): Representation of data, probability, discrete random variables, and normal distribution.
Probability & Statistics 2 (Paper 6 / S2): Poisson distribution, linear combinations of random variables, continuous random variables, sampling, and hypothesis testing.



2. Pearson Edexcel International A-Level (IAL)
Modular qualification structure comprising P1, P2, P3, P4 (Pure Mathematics), M1, M2 (Mechanics), S1, S2 (Statistics), and FP1–FP3 (Further Pure Mathematics).

title: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 2 (May 2026)
text:
Note📝 Thông Tin Đề Thi IB Math AA HL Paper 2 (May 2026)




Thời gian làm bài: 2 giờ (120 phút)
Tổng điểm: 110 marks
Quy định: Đội ngũ học sinh được phép sử dụng máy tính đồ họa (Graphic Display Calculator - GDC).
Cấu trúc: Section A (9 câu hỏi ngắn, 64 điểm) & Section B (3 câu hỏi mở rộng, 46 điểm).





Section A

Question 1 [Maximum mark: 7]
A group of 52 students have their heights measured in cm.

Use the cumulative frequency data to find an estimate of the median height. [2 marks]

The heights of the students are shown in the following frequency table where \(p, q \in \mathbb{N}\).



Height (\(h\) cm)
Frequency




\(155 \le h < 160\)
3


\(160 \le h < 165\)
8


\(165 \le h < 170\)
14


\(170 \le h < 175\)
\(p\)


\(175 \le h < 180\)
\(q\)





Find the value of \(p\) and the value of \(q\).
Use the frequency table to find an estimate of the mean height, giving your answer to four significant figures. [5 marks]





Question 2 [Maximum mark: 4]
Consider a function \(f\) which has a first derivative given by \(f'(x)=x^2-x-1\), where \(x \in \mathbb{R}\).
Find the range of values of \(x\) for which \(f\) is decreasing. [4 marks]



Question 3 [Maximum mark: 6]
A Ferris wheel with radius 20 metres rotates at a constant speed. The centre of the wheel is 23 metres above the ground. P is a point on the wheel.
The wheel starts moving with P at the lowest point and completes one revolution in 4 minutes.
The height, \(h\) metres, of P above the ground after \(t\) minutes is given by \(h=a-b\cos(ct)^\circ\), where \(a, b, c \in \mathbb{Z}^+\).

Find the value of \(a\), the value of \(b\) and the value of \(c\). [4 marks]

The height can also be given as \(h(t)=a-b\sin(c(t+d))^\circ\), where \(d \in \mathbb{Z}^+\).

Find the smallest positive value of \(d\). [2 marks]




Question 4 [Maximum mark: 7]
Consider the function \(g\) defined as \(g(x)=x^3-3x+2\sin x\), where \(x \in \mathbb{R}\).
The graph of \(g\) has a local maximum at point A and a local minimum at point B. The line (AB) passes through the origin O at (0,0).
The region R is enclosed by the graph of \(g\) and the line segment [OB].

Find the coordinates of point A and the coordinates of point B. [2 marks]
Find the area of R. [5 marks]




Question 5 [Maximum mark: 7]
A large group of adults have their heights measured. The heights of the adults are normally distributed with mean \(\mu\) cm and standard deviation \(\sigma\) cm.
The probability that one of the adults chosen at random has a height greater than 171 cm is 0.4.
If one of the adults with a height greater than 171 cm is chosen at random, the probability that their height is greater than 175 cm is 0.35.
Find the value of \(\mu\) and the value of \(\sigma\). [7 marks]



Question 6 [Maximum mark: 4]
The air inside an airtight syringe is compressed so that its volume, \(V \text{ cm}^3\), decreases.
The air pressure, \(P\) Newtons per \(\text{cm}^2\), within the syringe is inversely proportional to the volume so that \(PV=135\).
At a given time, the volume of air is \(20 \text{ cm}^3\) and is decreasing at a rate of \(8 \text{ cm}^3\) per minute.
Find the rate of increase in the air pressure at this time. [4 marks]



Question 7 [Maximum mark: 6]
The continuous random variable \(X\) has a probability distribution \(f\) defined as
\[f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{b}{a}x, & 0 \le x \le a \\ \frac{b}{a-5}(x-5), & a < x \le 5 \end{cases}\]
where \(0 < a < 5\) and \(b \in \mathbb{Q}^+\).

Show that \(b=0.4\). [2 marks]

It is given that \(\text{E}(X)=3.2\).

Find the value of \(a\). [4 marks]




Question 8 [Maximum mark: 8]
Consider the equation \(z^3=c\), where \(z \in \mathbb{C}\) and \(c\) is a positive constant.
One of the solutions of the equation is \(z=-2+2i\sqrt{3}\).

Find the value of \(c\). [2 marks]
Write down the other two solutions of \(z^3=c\) giving your answers in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\). [2 marks]
Find the solutions of \((iz)^3=c\) giving your answers in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\). [2 marks]

The solutions of \((iz)^3=c\) can be represented on an Argand diagram by three points A, B and C.

Find the area of the triangle ABC. [2 marks]




Question 9 [Maximum mark: 8]
Consider the curve \((x-d)^2+(y-2)^2=4\) where \(x, y \in \mathbb{R}\) and \(d>2\).
The region enclosed by the curve is rotated through \(2\pi\) radians around the y-axis to form a solid, S.

Show that the volume of S is given by \(4\pi d\int_{0}^{4}\sqrt{4-(y-2)^2}dy\). [6 marks]

It is given that the volume of S is \(50\pi^2 \text{ cm}^3\).

Find the value of \(d\). [2 marks]





Section B

Question 10 [Maximum mark: 13]
At the start of 2026, Lavinia receives a gift of \(\$15000\). She wants to buy a boat which costs \(\$28000\) so she decides to invest her money.
On 1 January 2026 Lavinia invests her money in a bank account which pays interest at a nominal annual rate of 4.8%, compounded quarterly. The interest is paid into her account on the last day of each quarter. She makes no further deposits to, or withdrawals from, the account.

Find the amount of money Lavinia will have in her bank account on 1 January 2031. Give your answer correct to the nearest dollar. [3 marks]
Show that Lavinia will first have more than \(\$28000\) in her bank account during the year 2039. [3 marks]

The cost of the boat at the start of 2026 was \(\$28000\), and it depreciates at a constant annual rate of \(r\%\). After one year the cost of the boat is \(\$26222\).

Find the value of \(r\). [2 marks]

Due to this depreciation, Lavinia will be able to buy the boat before 2039. She will buy the boat as soon as she has enough money in her bank account to pay for it.

Determine the year during which Lavinia will buy the boat. [5 marks]




Question 11 [Maximum mark: 19]
A child’s toy is made from a solid right cone and a solid hemisphere of equal radius. The circular faces of each solid are joined to form a single circle C. The point P lies on the circumference of C, and the point V is the vertex of the cone.
All units are given in cm.
The toy is positioned so that the circle C lies completely within the plane defined by \(x+2y-z=5\).
The point P has coordinates \((-3, 6, 4)\) and the point V has coordinates \((4, 16, -5)\).

Find a vector equation for the line passing through V and the centre of C. [3 marks]
Find the coordinates of the centre of C. [3 marks]

Show that the radius of C is \(\sqrt{14}\) cm.
Find the total surface area of the toy. [6 marks]


The toy is rotated so that the position of the vertex is fixed at V and the image \(P'\) of the point P has coordinates \((-9, 11, 1)\).

Find angle \(P\hat{V}P'\) giving your answer in degrees. [3 marks]
Find an equation of the plane containing the points P, V and \(P'\), giving your answer in the form \(ax+by+cz=d\), where \(a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{Z}\). [4 marks]




Question 12 [Maximum mark: 21]
The function \(f\) is defined as \(f(x)=\frac{x^2+ax+b}{x+1}\), where \(x \ne -1\) and \(a, b \in \mathbb{Z}\).
First consider the case where \(\lim_{x \to -1}f(x)\) is finite.


Show that \(b=a-1\).
Find \(\lim_{x \to -1}f(x)\) in terms of \(a\). [4 marks]


Now consider the case where the graph of \(f\) has a vertical asymptote, an oblique asymptote with equation \(y=x-4\), and at least one point of zero gradient.

Write down the equation of the vertical asymptote. [1 mark]
Show that \(a=-3\). [3 marks]
Show that \(b \ge -3\). [6 marks]
In the case where \(a=-3\) and \(b=1\)

sketch the graph of \(y=f(|x|)\), showing any asymptotes with their equations, the value of the intercept with the y-axis, and the coordinates of any local maximum or minimum points;
solve \(f(|x|) < f(x)\). [7 marks]

text:
📐 Essential Topics & Mathematical Concepts

1. Proof by Mathematical Induction (IB Math AA HL)
Proof by induction requires a clear three-step structure: establishing the base step (\(n=1\)), stating the inductive hypothesis (\(n=k\)), and completing the inductive step (\(n=k+1\)):
[ P(n): _{i=1}^{n} i^3 = ^2 n ^+ ]


2. Complex Numbers in Euler and Polar Form (IB Math AA HL)
Expressing complex numbers in exponential form simplifies multiplication, division, and applying De Moivre’s Theorem:
[ z = r(+ i) = r e^{i} z^n = r^n e^{in} ]


3. Differential Equations (IB Math AA/AI HL)
Solving first-order linear differential equations by integrating factors or separation of variables:
[ + P(x)y = Q(x) ]


4. Hypothesis Testing & Chi-Squared Tests (IB Math AI HL/SL)
Utilizing Graphic Display Calculators (GDC like Casio fx-CG50 or TI-Nspire CX II) to evaluate test statistics, degrees of freedom, and \(p\)-values against significance levels (\(\alpha = 0.05\)).


5. The Binomial Theorem (IB Math AA SL/HL)
Expanding expressions of the form \((a + b)^n\) using combination notation:
[ (a + b)^n = _{k=0}^{n} a^{n-k} b^k ]

title: A-Level Chemistry (CIE 9701 & Edexcel IAL) Study Guide for District 2 Students
text:
🔬 Key Branches of A-Level Chemistry

1. Physical Chemistry

Chemical Energetics: Constructing Born-Haber cycles to calculate lattice energies (\(\Delta H_{\text{lat}}^\theta\)) and hydration enthalpies.
Electrochemistry: Standard electrode potentials \(E^\theta\), the Nernst equation, and electrochemical cells.
Equilibria & Buffers: Calculating the pH of buffer solutions using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation:

[ = K_a + () ]


2. Inorganic Chemistry

Periodicity & Group Trends: Group 2 sulfates and hydroxides solubility trends; halogens oxidizing ability.
Transition Elements: Formation of complex ions, \(d\)-\(d\) orbital splitting, ligand exchange reactions, and variable oxidation states.



3. Organic Chemistry

Reaction Mechanisms: Electrophilic addition of alkenes, electrophilic substitution of benzene, and nucleophilic substitution of acyl chlorides.
Analytical Techniques: Interpreting \(^1\text{H}\) and \(^{13}\text{C}\) NMR spectra, Infra-Red (IR) spectroscopy, and Mass Spectrometry to elucidate unknown organic structures.

title: A-Level Chemistry (CIE 9701 & Edexcel IAL) Study Guide for District 2 Students

Paper 3 (Advanced Practical Skills): Focuses on volumetric analysis (titrations), enthalpy determination (calorimetry), and qualitative analysis of inorganic ions.
Paper 5 (Planning, Analysis and Evaluation): Focuses on experimental design, identifying variables, uncertainty evaluation, and graphical data analysis.

title: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 1 (May 2026)
text:
Note📝 Thông Tin Đề Thi IB Math AA HL Paper 1 (May 2026)




Thời gian làm bài: 2 giờ (120 phút)
Tổng điểm: 110 marks
Quy định: Không sử dụng máy tính bỏ túi (Non-Calculator Paper).
Cấu trúc: Section A (9 câu hỏi ngắn, 68 điểm) & Section B (3 câu hỏi mở rộng, 52 điểm).





Section A

Question 1 [Maximum mark: 5]
Consider the function \(f(x)=3(x-2)(x-q)\), where \(x \in \mathbb{R}\) and \(q\) is a real constant.
The axis of symmetry of the graph of \(f\) has equation \(x=4\).

Show that \(q=6\). [2 marks]
Find the coordinates of the vertex of the graph of \(f\). [2 marks]
Hence, write down the range of \(f\). [1 mark]




Question 2 [Maximum mark: 5]
A particle P is travelling along a straight line, with displacement measured relative to a point O on the line. The velocity, \(v \text{ m s}^{-1}\), of the particle at time \(t\) seconds is given by
\[v=\frac{1}{t+1}+e^{-t}\]
where \(t \ge 0\).

Find \(\int\left(\frac{1}{t+1}+e^{-t}\right)dt\). [2 marks]

Initially the particle is at O.

Find an expression for the displacement, \(s\) metres, in terms of \(t\). [3 marks]




Question 3 [Maximum mark: 6]
Consider a geometric sequence, \(u_n\), with common ratio \(r\), where each term in the sequence is positive.
It is given that \(u_6=1.6 \times 10^5\) and \(u_8=6.4 \times 10^5\).

Find the value of \(r\). [3 marks]
Find the value of \(u_1\), giving your answer in the form \(a \times 10^k\), where \(1 \le a < 10\) and \(k \in \mathbb{Z}\). [3 marks]




Question 4 [Maximum mark: 7]

Show that \(\log_{25}(81x^2)=\log_5{9}+\log_5{x}\) for \(x>0\). [4 marks]
Hence, solve the equation \(\log_5{\sqrt[3]{x}}=\log_{25}(81x^2)-\log_5{4}\) where \(x>0\). [3 marks]




Question 5 [Maximum mark: 9]
Consider two events, A and B.
It is given that \(P(A' \cap B)=\frac{1}{6}\), \(P(A \cap B)=\frac{7-x}{12}\) and \(P(A \cap B')=\frac{5+x}{24}\), where \(0 \le x \le 7\).

Show that \(P(A)=\frac{19-x}{24}\). [3 marks]

It is given that A and B are independent.

Find the possible values of \(x\). [6 marks]




Question 6 [Maximum mark: 4]
Consider a piece of paper in the shape of a circle with centre O and radius \(r\) cm, where \(r>6\). A second circle with centre O and radius 6 cm is drawn inside the first and shaded.
The points A and B are on the circumference of the larger circle such that the acute angle \(A\hat{O}B=\frac{\pi}{3}\). The paper is cut along the lines AO and BO and the sector AOB with a central angle of \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) is removed.
After removing the sector, it is now given that
\[\frac{\text{the area of the unshaded region}}{\text{the area of the shaded region}}=\frac{2}{3}\]
Find the value of \(r\), giving your answer in the form \(\sqrt{k}\), where \(k \in \mathbb{Z}\).



Question 7 [Maximum mark: 6]
Reyn is investigating the fertility of a group of adult female foxes. He has developed a clinical test that aims to identify whether or not a given fox is pregnant, and he wants to evaluate the reliability of this test.
Reyn knows that:

40% of the foxes in the group are pregnant
if a fox is pregnant, the probability that it will test positive is 90%
if a fox is not pregnant, the probability it will test positive is 20%.


Find the probability that a randomly selected fox from the group will test positive. [3 marks]
Find the probability that a randomly selected fox from the group is pregnant, given that it tested positive. [3 marks]




Question 8 [Maximum mark: 8]
Consider the polynomial \(p(z)=3z^5-7z^4+cz^3+dz^2+ez-26\) where \(z \in \mathbb{C}\) and \(c, d, e \in \mathbb{R}\).
Three of the roots of \(p(z)\) are \(\frac{1}{3}\), \(a-i\), \(2+bi\), where \(a, b \in \mathbb{R}\), \(b>1\).

By considering the sum and the product of the roots of \(p(z)\),

show that \(a=-1\);
find the value of \(b\). [5 marks]

Show that \(p(z)=(Az+B)(z^2+Cz+D)(z^2+Ez+F)\), where \(A, B, C, D, E, F\) are integers to be determined. [3 marks]




Question 9 [Maximum mark: 8]
Consider non-zero vectors \(\mathbf{a}\), \(\mathbf{b}\) and \(\mathbf{c}\) in three-dimensional space.
The non-zero vector \(\mathbf{v}\) is defined as \(\mathbf{v}=(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{c})\mathbf{b}-(\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b})\mathbf{c}\).

Show that \(\mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{a}=0\). [2 marks]

It is given that \(\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}\) and \(\mathbf{a} \times (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c})\) are non-zero vectors.


Justify why \(\mathbf{b} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c})=0\).
Show that \(\mathbf{v} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c})=0\). [4 marks]

Hence, state the geometrical relationship between \(\mathbf{v}\) and \(\mathbf{a} \times (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c})\), briefly justifying your answer. [2 marks]





Section B

Question 10 [Maximum mark: 15]
Consider the function \(f(x)=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d\), where \(x \in \mathbb{R}\) and where \(a, b, c\) and \(d\) are real constants.
The graph of \(f\) has a point of inflexion at \((-2,-2c+d+24)\).

Show that \(a=\frac{3}{2}\) and \(b=9\). [6 marks]

It is given that the tangents to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=-3\) and \(x=k\) are horizontal.


Show that \(c=\frac{27}{2}\).
Find the value of \(k\).
State whether \(f\) has a local maximum or a local minimum at \(x=k\), justifying your answer. [7 marks]


The graph of \(f\) intersects the y-axis at the point P.

Show that the tangent to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=-3\) passes through P. [2 marks]




Question 11 [Maximum mark: 19]

Prove the identity \(\cot{2\theta} \equiv \frac{1}{2}\left(\cot{\theta}-\frac{1}{\cot{\theta}}\right)\). [3 marks]
Hence, solve the equation \(\cot{2\theta}=\frac{3}{2}\cot{\theta}(\cot^2{\theta}-1)\) for \(0 < \theta < \pi\) where \(\theta \ne \frac{\pi}{2}\). [6 marks]
By differentiating both sides of the identity in part (a), show that \(4\csc^2{2\theta} \equiv \csc^2{\theta}+\sec^2{\theta}\). [5 marks]

Consider the right-angled triangle \(\Delta PQR\), where \(R\hat{P}Q=\frac{\pi}{2}\), \(PR=\csc{\theta}\) and \(QR=2\csc{2\theta}\), where \(0 < \theta < \frac{\pi}{2}\) and all lengths are given in metres.
QR has length \(L\) metres and \(\Delta PQR\) has area \(A\) square metres.

Calculate the ratio \(L:A\) in the form \(n:1\) where \(n \in \mathbb{Z}^+\). [5 marks]




Question 12 [Maximum mark: 18]
Rowan is investigating the spread of an infection through a population of rabbits. He models \(N\), the number (in thousands) of infected rabbits in the population, at time \(t\) days.
Rowan models the spread of the infection by the differential equation
\[\frac{dN}{dt}=k(-3+4N-N^2)\]
where \(t \ge 0\) and \(k \in \mathbb{R}^+\).
Initially, 1500 rabbits are infected.

Express \(\frac{1}{-3+4x-x^2}\) in the form \(\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{B}{3-x}\), where \(A, B \in \mathbb{R}\). [3 marks]
Hence, show that \(\ln\left(\frac{N-1}{3-N}\right)=2kt-\ln{p}\), where \(p \in \mathbb{R}^+\) is a constant to be determined. [8 marks]
Find an expression for \(N\) in the form \(N=\frac{a+be^{-2kt}}{1+ce^{-2kt}}\) where \(a, b, c \in \mathbb{Z}\). [5 marks]

According to Rowan’s model, the number of infected rabbits approaches a limit, \(L\), over the long term.

Find the value of \(L\). [2 marks]

text:
Note🧪 IB Chemistry Academic Support in Thao Dien, District 2



This study guide is tailored for students pursuing the IB Diploma Program (IB DP) at international schools in District 2, Ho Chi Minh City — such as British International School (BIS), International School Ho Chi Minh City (ISHCMC), and European International School (EIS).
To help students build a solid conceptual foundation, NKK-Education Hub offers organized access to 546 IB Chemistry past paper files, topical revision worksheets, and reference guides curated by Dr. Kiem Nguyen.

title: IB Chemistry (HL & SL) Study Guide & Syllabus Breakdown for International Students in District 2
section: 🔬 Understanding the New IB Chemistry Curriculum Framework (2025+)
text:
🔬 Understanding the New IB Chemistry Curriculum Framework (2025+)
The current IB Chemistry syllabus organizes physical, inorganic, and organic chemistry into two interconnected themes: Structure and Reactivity.

1. Theme: Structure

Structure 1: Models of the particulate nature of matter (Kinetic molecular theory, gas laws).
Structure 2: Atomic structure (Mass spectrometry, electron configurations, emission spectra).
Structure 3: Counting particles by mass - The mole concept (Stoichiometry, limiting reactants, molar volume).
Structure 4: Periodicity & Bonding (VSEPR theory, intermolecular forces, metallic and ionic lattices).



2. Theme: Reactivity

Reactivity 1: What drives chemical reactions? (Thermodynamics, enthalpy changes \(\Delta H\), entropy \(\Delta S\), Gibbs free energy \(\Delta G\)).
Reactivity 2: How fast do chemical reactions go? (Kinetics, rate equations, reaction mechanisms, \(S_N1\) vs. \(S_N2\)).
Reactivity 3: How far do chemical reactions go? (Equilibrium constants \(K_c\), Le Chatelier’s principle, electrochemical cells \(E^\theta\)).

title: IB Chemistry (HL & SL) Study Guide & Syllabus Breakdown for International Students in District 2
text:
⚗️ Key Chemical Concepts & Mathematical Formulas

1. Gibbs Free Energy & Spontaneity (\(\Delta G^\theta\))
[ G^= H^- TS^ ]
A reaction is thermodynamically spontaneous when \(\Delta G^\theta < 0\). Remember to convert \(\Delta S^\theta\) from \(\text{J}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\) to \(\text{kJ}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\).


2. The Arrhenius Equation & Activation Energy (\(E_a\))
[ k = A e^{-} k = - () + A ]
Plotting \(\ln k\) against \(\frac{1}{T}\) yields a straight line with a gradient of \(-\frac{E_a}{R}\).


3. Nucleophilic Substitution Mechanisms (\(S_N1\) vs. \(S_N2\))

\(S_N1\): Two-step mechanism involving a carbocation intermediate; favored by tertiary halogenoalkanes. Rate equation: \(\text{Rate} = k[\text{R-X}]\).
\(S_N2\): One-step concerted mechanism involving a transition state; favored by primary halogenoalkanes. Rate equation: \(\text{Rate} = k[\text{R-X}][\text{Nu}^-]\).

section: 📊 Thống kê chi tiết kho đề thi IB
text:
📊 Thống kê chi tiết kho đề thi IB

Hiện tại, trang IB Chemistry Overview đã lưu trữ tổng cộng 546 tệp đề thi (QP) và đáp án (MS) chính thức:

Higher Level (HL): 270 tệp
Standard Level (SL): 276 tệp

Analysis & Approaches (AA) HL: 106 tệp
Analysis & Approaches (AA) SL: 76 tệp
Applications & Interpretation (AI) HL: 96 tệp
Applications & Interpretation (AI) SL: 76 tệp (Trong đó vừa bổ sung và chuẩn hóa 34 tệp mới thuộc kỳ thi 2025 Winter cho cả 4 phân môn).

Bao gồm đầy đủ các môn: Math HL, Math SL, Math Studies, Further Math HL/SL cùng các môn chuyên đề HL Options (Calculus, Statistics, Discrete Math, Sets & Groups).

NoteCourse Portal: CIE IGCSE Mathematics (0580)



Welcome, students! This specialized academic portal provides in-depth resources for the Cambridge International GCSE Mathematics (0580) curriculum. Here, you will find exhaustive syllabus checklists, revision notes, targeted practice question banks, and official exam information—all mathematically formatted to optimize your learning and help you achieve an A*.

title: CIE IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
text:
1. Course Introduction

Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) is a structured and comprehensive academic curriculum designed to develop mathematical skills, logical thinking, and problem-solving capabilities. The syllabus is divided into two tiers of entry: Core Tier (eligible for grades C–G) and Extended Tier (eligible for grades A*–E), offering appropriate routes of assessment for students of different abilities.


Assessment Outline





Paper Number


Tier


Assessment Information


Marks


Weighting






Paper 1 (Core)


Core


Assessed through a 1 hour 30 minutes examination set and marked by Cambridge. Use of a calculator is not allowed. Weighted at 50% of the qualification, eligible for grades C to G.


80 marks


50%




Paper 3 (Core)


Core


Assessed through a 1 hour 30 minutes examination set and marked by Cambridge. A scientific calculator is required. Weighted at 50% of the qualification, eligible for grades C to G.


80 marks


50%




Paper 2 (Extended)


Extended


Assessed through a 2-hour examination set and marked by Cambridge. Use of a calculator is not allowed. Weighted at 50% of the qualification, eligible for grades A* to E.


100 marks


50%




Paper 4 (Extended)


Extended


Assessed through a 2-hour examination set and marked by Cambridge. A scientific calculator is required. Weighted at 50% of the qualification, eligible for grades A* to E.


100 marks


50%





Assessment Objectives (AOs) Weightings: * AO1 (Knowledge and understanding of mathematical techniques): Core 60–70% | Extended 40–50% * AO2 (Analyse, interpret and communicate mathematically): Core 30–40% | Extended 50–60%


Syllabus Structure

The Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics syllabus content is categorized into 9 major topics, covering core concepts for all students with extended high-level parts for the Extended Tier:







Note1 Number





1.1 Types of number 1.2 Sets 1.3 Powers and roots 1.4 Fractions, decimals and percentages 1.5 Ordering 1.6 The four operations 1.7 Indices I 1.8 Standard form 1.9 Estimation 1.10 Limits of accuracy 1.11 Ratio and proportion 1.12 Rates 1.13 Percentages 1.14 Using a calculator 1.15 Time 1.16 Money 1.17 Exponential growth and decay (Extended only) 1.18 Surds (Extended only)









Note2 Algebra and graphs





2.1 Introduction to algebra 2.2 Algebraic manipulation 2.3 Algebraic fractions (Extended only) 2.4 Indices II 2.5 Equations 2.6 Inequalities 2.7 Sequences 2.8 Proportion (Extended only) 2.9 Graphs in practical situations 2.10 Graphs of functions 2.11 Sketching curves 2.12 Differentiation (Extended only) 2.13 Functions (Extended only)









Note3 Coordinate geometry





3.1 Coordinates 3.2 Drawing linear graphs 3.3 Gradient of linear graphs 3.4 Length and midpoint (Extended only) 3.5 Equations of linear graphs 3.6 Parallel lines 3.7 Perpendicular lines (Extended only)









Note4 Geometry





4.1 Geometrical terms 4.2 Geometrical constructions 4.3 Scale drawings 4.4 Similarity 4.5 Symmetry 4.6 Angles 4.7 Circle theorems I 4.8 Circle theorems II (Extended only)









Note5 Mensuration





5.1 Units of measure 5.2 Area and perimeter 5.3 Circles, arcs and sectors 5.4 Surface area and volume 5.5 Compound shapes and parts of shapes









Note6 Trigonometry





6.1 Pythagoras’ theorem 6.2 Right-angled triangles 6.3 Exact trigonometric values (Extended only) 6.4 Trigonometric functions (Extended only) 6.5 Non-right-angled triangles (Extended only) 6.6 Pythagoras’ theorem and trigonometry in 3D (Extended only)









Note7 Transformations and vectors





7.1 Transformations 7.2 Vectors in two dimensions (Extended only) 7.3 Magnitude of a vector (Extended only) 7.4 Vector geometry (Extended only)









Note8 Probability





8.1 Introduction to probability 8.2 Relative and expected frequencies 8.3 Probability of combined events 8.4 Conditional probability (Extended only)









Note9 Statistics





9.1 Classifying statistical data 9.2 Interpreting statistical data 9.3 Averages and measures of spread 9.4 Statistical charts and diagrams 9.5 Scatter diagrams 9.6 Cumulative frequency diagrams (Extended only) 9.7 Histograms (Extended only)

A-Level Assessment Routes


AS Level Award: Typically taken in the first year, combining 2 papers (Paper 1 + one of Paper 2, 4, or 5).


Full A-Level Award: Compiled from 4 papers. The three standard routes are:


Route 1: Paper 1, Paper 3, Paper 4 (Mechanics), and Paper 5 (Probability & Statistics 1). (Most common)


Route 2: Paper 1, Paper 3, Paper 5 (Probability & Statistics 1), and Paper 6 (Probability & Statistics 2).


Route 3: Paper 1, Paper 3, Paper 4 (Mechanics), and Paper 6 (Probability & Statistics 2). (Requires Route 1 / Mechanics knowledge)

NoteAcademic Portal: Cambridge International AS & A Level Further Mathematics (9231)



Welcome to the official study portal for Cambridge International AS & A Level Further Mathematics (9231). This rigorous, higher-level curriculum is designed for high-achieving mathematics students preparing for university degrees in Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, and Theoretical Physics at elite institutions worldwide (such as Cambridge, Oxford, Imperial, MIT, and Ivy League universities).

title: CIE A-Level Further Mathematics
text:
1. Course Introduction

Cambridge International AS & A Level Further Mathematics (9231) extends mathematical understanding beyond standard A-Level Mathematics (9709), introducing advanced university-level concepts including Proof by Mathematical Induction, Linear Spaces, Matrix Transformations, Polar Coordinates, Complex Numbers, Second-order Differential Equations, Non-linear Mechanics, and Advanced Inferential Statistics.


Assessment Structure

The 9231 qualification comprises four specialized papers. Candidates can achieve either a Cambridge International AS Level (2 papers) or a full Cambridge International A Level (all 4 papers).











Paper Component
Duration & Marks
Curriculum Content & Calculator Policy
A-Level Weighting




Paper 1: Further Pure Mathematics 1
2 hours
75 marks
Polynomial Roots, Rational Functions & Graphs, Summation of Series, Matrices & 2D/3D Linear Transformations, Polar Coordinates ($r = f(\theta)$), Vectors in 3D Space, Proof by Induction. Calculator permitted.
30%
(60% of AS)


Paper 2: Further Pure Mathematics 2
2 hours
75 marks
Hyperbolic Functions, Maclaurin & Taylor Series, Arc Length & Surface Area of Revolution, Linear Spaces (Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, Diagonalisation), Complex Numbers (de Moivre’s Theorem, $n^{\text{th}}$ Roots of Unity), Second-order Differential Equations ($a y’’ + b y’ + c y = f(x)$). Calculator permitted.
30%
(A-Level only)


Paper 3: Further Mechanics
1 hr 30 mins
50 marks
Motion of a Projectile, Equilibrium of a Rigid Body, Circular Motion, Hooke’s Law (Elastic Strings & Springs), Linear Motion under a Variable Force, Momentum in 2D (Oblique Elastic/Inelastic Collisions). Calculator permitted.
20%
(40% of AS)


Paper 4: Further Probability & Statistics
1 hr 30 mins
50 marks
Continuous Random Variables, Sampling & Estimation ($t$-distribution), $\chi^2$-Tests for Independence and Goodness of Fit, Non-parametric Tests (Single-sample Sign Test, Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test), Probability Generating Functions (PGFs). Calculator permitted.
20%
(40% of AS)






Routes to Certification

Candidates can choose between two official Cambridge assessment routes depending on their academic pathways:










Certification Route
Required Paper Combinations
Assessment Details & Progression




AS Level Further Mathematics
2 Papers
Option 1: Paper 1 (FP1) + Paper 3 (FM)
Option 2: Paper 1 (FP1) + Paper 4 (FS)
Awarded with grades A through E. Provides foundational knowledge in university-level pure mathematics alongside either mechanics or advanced statistics.


Full A Level Further Mathematics
All 4 Papers
Compulsory 4-Paper Linear / Staged:
Paper 1 (FP1) + Paper 2 (FP2) + Paper 3 (FM) + Paper 4 (FS)
Awarded with grades A* through E. Candidates can sit all 4 papers in a single terminal exam series, or carry forward their AS Level results from Year 1 to complete the full A-Level.

text:
NoteRoad to Achieving an A* in Edexcel A-Level Mathematics



Welcome, students! Pearson Edexcel International Advanced Level (IAL) Mathematics is a flexible modular curriculum. NKK-Education Hub provides a structured library of core study notes, topical worksheets, and actual exam past papers organized by individual exam units to help you optimize your learning and achieve an A* grade.

title: Edexcel Mathematics Overview
text:
1. Course Introduction

Pearson Edexcel International Advanced Level in Mathematics follows a modular design, enabling candidates to take examinations throughout the course. The qualification is built from different units, allowing students to specialize in areas of Pure Mathematics, Mechanics, Statistics, or Decision Mathematics.


Assessment Outline

To obtain an International Advanced Level (IAL) in Mathematics, candidates must Cash-In six modules, including the compulsory Pure Mathematics units (P1, P2, P3, P4) plus two optional application units.






Exam Module


Syllabus Component


Format & Duration


Marks


IAL Weighting






Pure Mathematics 1 (P1)


Algebra, coordinate geometry, trig, calculus


Written exam — 1 hour 30 minutes


75 marks


16.7% (33.3% of IAS)




Pure Mathematics 2 (P2)


Proof, sequences, exponentials, logs, circle


Written exam — 1 hour 30 minutes


75 marks


16.7% (33.3% of IAS)




Pure Mathematics 3 (P3)


Inverse trig, algebraic methods, advanced calculus


Written exam — 1 hour 30 minutes


75 marks


16.7% (16.7% of IAL)




Pure Mathematics 4 (P4)


Parametrics, partial fractions, vectors, integration


Written exam — 1 hour 30 minutes


75 marks


16.7% (16.7% of IAL)




Optional Unit 1 (e.g., S1 / M1)


Probability and statistics or basic mechanics


Written exam — 1 hour 30 minutes


75 marks


16.7%




Optional Unit 2 (e.g., S2 / M2 / D1)


Advanced statistics, dynamics, or decision math


Written exam — 1 hour 30 minutes


75 marks


16.7%







Cash-In and Grading Criteria


IAS Level Award: Compiled from 3 units (P1, P2 + one application unit like S1 or M1). The maximum raw marks are converted to a Uniform Mark Scale (UMS) maximum of 300 UMS.


IAL Level Award: Compiled from 6 units (P1, P2, P3, P4 + two application units) with a maximum of 600 UMS marks.


A* Criteria: To achieve an A* grade overall, candidates must score at least 480 UMS marks in total across the 6 units, and score at least 180 out of 200 UMS marks on P3 and P4 combined.




Syllabus Structure

The core units of the Edexcel IAL Mathematics curriculum comprise the following detailed topics:








NoteP1: Pure Mathematics 1






1. Algebra and functions
1.1 Laws of indices. 1.2 Surds. 1.3 Quadratic functions and graphs. 1.4 Discriminant. 1.5 Completing the square & solving quadratics. 1.6 Simultaneous equations. 1.7 Interpret inequalities graphically. 1.8 Represent inequalities graphically. 1.9 Solutions of inequalities. 1.10 Algebraic manipulation of polynomials. 1.11 Cubic and reciprocal functions. 1.12 Graph transformations.


2. Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
2.1 Equation of a straight line. 2.2 Parallel and perpendicular lines.


3. Trigonometry
3.1 Sine rule, cosine rule and triangle area. 3.2 Radian measure. 3.3 Sine, cosine and tangent functions.


4. Differentiation
4.1 The derivative and rates of change. 4.2 Differentiation of polynomials. 4.3 Gradients, tangents and normals.


5. Integration
5.1 Indefinite integration. 5.2 Integration of polynomials.










NoteP2: Pure Mathematics 2






1. Proof
1.1 Structure of mathematical proof. 1.2 Proof by exhaustion. 1.3 Disproof by counter example.


2. Algebra and functions
2.1 Algebraic division, Factor and Remainder Theorems.


3. Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
3.1 Coordinate geometry of the circle.


4. Sequences and series
4.1 Sequences. 4.2 Arithmetic sequences and series. 4.3 Increasing, decreasing and periodic sequences. 4.4 Geometric sequences and series. 4.5 Binomial expansion.


5. Exponentials and logarithms
5.1 Exponential functions and graphs. 5.2 Laws of logarithms. 5.3 Solving exponential equations.


6. Trigonometry
6.1 Trigonometric identities. 6.2 Solving trigonometric equations.


7. Differentiation
7.1 Maxima, minima and stationary points.


8. Integration
8.1 Definite integrals. 8.2 Area under a curve. 8.3 Trapezium rule.










NoteP3: Pure Mathematics 3






1. Algebra and functions
1.1 Simplification of rational expressions. 1.2 Functions and inverse functions. 1.3 Modulus function. 1.4 Combinations of transformations.


2. Trigonometry
2.1 Secant, cosecant, cotangent and inverse trig functions. 2.2 Pythagorean identities. 2.3 Addition and double angle formulae.


3. Exponential and logarithms
3.1 The exponential function. 3.2 The natural logarithm function. 3.3 Logarithmic graphs and relationships.


4. Differentiation
4.1 Differentiating exponential, log and trig functions. 4.2 Product, quotient and chain rules. 4.3 Differentiating inverse relations. 4.4 Exponential growth and decay.


5. Integration
5.1 Integrating standard functions. 5.2 Integration by recognition.


6. Numerical methods
6.1 Location of roots. 6.2 Simple iterative methods.










NoteP4: Pure Mathematics 4






1. Proof
1.1 Proof by contradiction.


2. Algebra and functions
2.1 Partial fractions.


3. Coordinate geometry in the (x, y) plane
3.1 Parametric equations.


4. Binomial expansion
4.1 Binomial series for rational powers.


5. Differentiation
5.1 Implicit and parametric differentiation. 5.2 Simple differential equations.


6. Integration
6.1 Volume of revolution. 6.2 Integration by substitution and parts. 6.3 Integration using partial fractions. 6.4 Solving first order differential equations. 6.5 Area under parametric curves.


7. Vectors
7.1 2D and 3D vectors. 7.2 Magnitude of a vector. 7.3 Vector algebra. 7.4 Position vectors. 7.5 Distance between two points. 7.6 Vector equations of lines. 7.7 Scalar product and angles between lines.










NoteM1: Mechanics 1






1. Mathematical models in mechanics
1.1 Basic ideas of mathematical modelling.


2. Vectors in mechanics
2.1 Magnitude and direction. 2.2 Applying vectors to kinematics and forces.


3. Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line
3.1 Constant acceleration.


4. Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane
4.1 Newton’s laws of motion. 4.2 Connected particles. 4.3 Momentum, impulse and conservation of momentum. 4.4 Coefficient of friction.


5. Statics of a particle
5.1 Resolution of forces. 5.2 Equilibrium of a particle. 5.3 Friction in equilibrium.


6. Moments
6.1 Moment of a force.










NoteM2: Mechanics 2






1. Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane
1.1 Motion under gravity. 1.2 Projectiles. 1.3 Variable acceleration.


2. Centres of mass
2.1 Centre of mass of discrete distributions. 2.2 Centre of mass of plane figures. 2.3 Equilibrium of a plane lamina.


3. Work and energy
3.1 Kinetic/potential energy, work, power and conservation.


4. Collisions
4.1 Impulse and conservation of momentum in vectors. 4.2 Direct impact and restitution.


5. Statics of rigid bodies
5.1 Moment of a force. 5.2 Equilibrium of rigid bodies.










NoteS1: Statistics 1






1. Mathematical models in probability and statistics
1.1 Basic ideas of mathematical modelling.


2. Representation and summary of data
2.1 Histograms, stem/leaf diagrams, box plots. 2.2 Measures of location. 2.3 Measures of dispersion. 2.4 Skewness and outliers.


3. Probability
3.1 Elementary and conditional probability. 3.2 Probability rules. 3.3 Independence. 3.4 Sum and product laws.


4. Correlation and regression
4.1 Scatter diagrams and linear regression. 4.2 Explanatory and response variables. 4.3 Product moment correlation coefficient.


5. Discrete random variables
5.1 Concept of a discrete random variable. 5.2 Probability and cumulative distribution functions. 5.3 Mean and variance. 5.4 Discrete uniform distribution.


6. The Normal distribution
6.1 The Normal distribution and cumulative tables.










NoteS2: Statistics 2






1. The Binomial and Poisson distributions
1.1 Binomial and Poisson distributions. 1.2 Mean and variance. 1.3 Poisson approximation to binomial.


2. Continuous random variables
2.1 Concept of a continuous random variable. 2.2 PDF and CDF. 2.3 Relationship between density and distribution. 2.4 Mean and variance. 2.5 Mode, median and quartiles.


3. Continuous distributions
3.1 Continuous uniform distribution. 3.2 Normal approximations.


4. Hypothesis tests
4.1 Population, census and sample. 4.2 Statistic and sampling distribution. 4.3 Null and alternative hypotheses. 4.4 Critical region. 4.5 One-tailed and two-tailed tests. 4.6 Tests for binomial and Poisson distributions.

title: Edexcel Pure Mathematics 3
text:
1. Syllabus
The detailed syllabus structure for Edexcel Pure Mathematics 3 (P3) comprises the following topics:


1. Algebra and functions
1.1 Simplification of rational expressions. 1.2 Functions and inverse functions. 1.3 Modulus function. 1.4 Combinations of transformations.


2. Trigonometry
2.1 Secant, cosecant, cotangent and inverse trig functions. 2.2 Pythagorean identities. 2.3 Addition and double angle formulae.


3. Exponential and logarithms
3.1 The exponential function. 3.2 The natural logarithm function. 3.3 Logarithmic graphs and relationships.


4. Differentiation
4.1 Differentiating exponential, log and trig functions. 4.2 Product, quotient and chain rules. 4.3 Differentiating inverse relations. 4.4 Exponential growth and decay.


5. Integration
5.1 Integrating standard functions. 5.2 Integration by recognition.


6. Numerical methods
6.1 Location of roots. 6.2 Simple iterative methods.

title: IB Mathematics AA HL
text:
1. Course Introduction

Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (AA) Higher Level (HL) focuses on developing strong analytical and rational thinking skills. The course emphasizes rigorous mathematical proofs, algebraic methods, and deep concepts of calculus and algebraic analysis. It is highly recommended for students aiming to study Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, or Mathematics at premier universities worldwide.


Assessment Outline

The IB Mathematics AA HL course is assessed through final written examinations (80%) and an independent mathematical exploration task (20%). A graphic display calculator (GDC) is required only for Paper 2 and Paper 3:

Syllabus Structure

The syllabus is organized into five core topics consisting of both standard core content and advanced high-level extension topics (SL Core & HL Extensions):







NoteTopic 1: Number and algebra





1.1: Operations in standard form 1.2: Arithmetic sequences and series 1.3: Geometric sequences and series 1.4: Financial applications 1.5: Laws of exponents and logarithms 1.6: Simple deductive proofs 1.7: Rational exponents 1.8: Infinite geometric series 1.9: Binomial theorem 1.10: Permutations and combinations [AHL] 1.11: Partial fractions [AHL] 1.12: Complex numbers in Cartesian form [AHL] 1.13: Polar and Euler forms of complex numbers [AHL] 1.14: Conjugate roots of polynomials [AHL] 1.15: Proof by mathematical induction [AHL] 1.16: Systems of linear equations [AHL]









NoteTopic 2: Functions





2.1: Straight lines: equations, gradient, intercepts 2.2: Concept of a function: domain, range, notation 2.3: Graphs of functions 2.4: Key features of graphs 2.5: Composite and inverse functions 2.6: Quadratic functions and their graphs 2.7: Quadratic equations and discriminant 2.8: Reciprocal functions and graphs 2.9: Exponential and logarithmic functions 2.10: Solving equations graphically and analytically 2.11: Transformations of graphs 2.12: Factor and remainder theorems [AHL] 2.13: Rational functions [AHL] 2.14: Odd and even functions [AHL] 2.15: Solving inequalities [AHL] 2.16: Advanced graph transformations and modulus functions [AHL]









NoteTopic 3: Geometry and trigonometry





3.1: Distance and midpoint in 3D space 3.2: Right-angled trigonometry 3.3: Sine and cosine rules, area of a triangle 3.4: Radian measure, arc length, sector area 3.5: Unit circle trig definitions 3.6: Pythagorean identity and double angle formulae 3.7: Trigonometric graphs 3.8: Solving trigonometric equations 3.9: Reciprocal trigonometric functions [AHL] 3.10: Compound and double angle identities [AHL] 3.11: Vectors: position, displacement, magnitude [AHL] 3.12: Scalar product of vectors [AHL] 3.13: Vector product of vectors [AHL] 3.14: Vector equations of lines in 2D and 3D [AHL] 3.15: Line intersections in 3D [AHL] 3.16: Kinematics applications of vectors [AHL] 3.17: Vector equations of planes [AHL] 3.18: Intersections of lines and planes, intersections of planes [AHL]









NoteTopic 4: Statistics and probability





4.1: Population, sampling, discrete and continuous data 4.2: Data presentation: frequency tables, histograms, box plots 4.3: Measures of central tendency and dispersion 4.4: Linear correlation of bivariate data 4.5: Probability of events, Venn and tree diagrams 4.6: Independent and mutually exclusive events 4.7: Discrete random variables and expectation 4.8: Binomial distribution 4.9: Normal distribution 4.10: Regression line and predictions 4.11: Conditional probability 4.12: Standardized normal variables (z-scores) 4.13: Bayes’ theorem [AHL] 4.14: Probability density functions for continuous random variables [AHL]









NoteTopic 5: Calculus





5.1: Concept of limits 5.2: Increasing and decreasing functions 5.3: Derivative of power functions and basic rules 5.4: Tangents and normals equations 5.5: Indefinite integration as anti-differentiation 5.6: Derivative rules: product, quotient, and chain rules 5.7: Second derivative, concavity, points of inflection 5.8: Local maximum and minimum points 5.9: Kinematic applications 5.10: Indefinite integrals of standard functions 5.11: Definite integrals and area under a curve 5.12: Continuity and differentiability at a point [AHL] 5.13: Limits of indeterminate forms and L’Hopital’s rule [AHL] 5.14: Implicit differentiation and related rates [AHL] 5.15: Derivatives of reciprocal and inverse trig functions [AHL] 5.16: Integration by substitution and parts [AHL] 5.17: Volumes of revolution [AHL] 5.18: First-order differential equations [AHL] 5.19: Maclaurin series expansions [AHL]
